changes.summary: Imported Toolbar (Wave 5 Dioxus-only extra, task 4.6, sub-batch 1) unmodified except for the doc-example import path change from dioxus_primitives::toolbar to adico_primitives::toolbar. Reuses this crate's existing private collection module (already imported for Select in M1) for roving focus; no document::eval, portal, or DOM measurement API, so it is SSR-safe by construction and needed no target-gated adapter work.

Imported VirtualList (Wave 5 Dioxus-only extra, task 4.6, sub-batch 2), including its private virtual/{mod,types,utils,virtualizer}.rs support modules. virtual/{mod,types,utils,virtualizer}.rs port unmodified except for the doc-example import path change. virtual_list.rs's scroll/resize bridge was NOT ported as upstream wrote it: live Playwright testing (not just cargo check) found upstream's long-lived document::eval scroll subscription never registers in this Dioxus 0.7.9/0.7.10 web runtime -- the exact defect class docs/adico/m3-wave3-migration.md already recorded for use_global_escape_listener/use_outside_dismiss -- so VirtualList always rendered zero items (viewport_size stayed 0). Following that record's own fix pattern (native Dioxus event instead of root-causing the interpreter bug), the bridge was rewritten using native onscroll (dioxus::html::events::ScrollData, which already exposes scroll_top/client_height) and onmounted/MountedData for initial measurement and programmatic scroll correction -- the same MountedData API already used unconditionally elsewhere in this crate (move_interaction.rs, checkbox.rs, slider.rs), needing no web/desktop feature gate at all. This removed the serde/ScrollMsg JS-payload plumbing entirely (serde was added and then removed from adico-primitives's Cargo.toml in the same sub-batch) and is a strictly more reliable implementation of upstream's own documented behavior on every target: web, desktop, and native/server (which never fires a real scroll event and renders zero items, matching upstream's own unstyled/empty-until-interactive contract, not a capability loss).

Imported TagGroup/TagGroupMulti/TagGroupLabel/TagList/TagGroupEmpty/TagOption/TagRemoveButton (Wave 5 Dioxus-only extra, task 4.6, sub-batch 3) unmodified except for the doc-example import path change. Confirmed by reading the actual upstream source (not just the migration queue's one-line dependency note) that it composes only this crate's existing private collection/selectable/selection modules already imported for Select in M1; no document::eval, portal, or DOM measurement API anywhere in the module, so it is SSR-safe by construction and needed no target-gated adapter work.

Imported DragAndDropList/DragAndDropListItems/DragAndDropListItem/DragAndDropDropIndicator/DragAndDropInstructions/DragAndDropLiveRegion/use_drag_and_drop_list_items (Wave 5 Dioxus-only extra, task 4.6, sub-batch 4) unmodified except for the doc-example import path change and one structural adaptation: `DragAndDropListItem`'s `ondragstart` handler registered a `document::eval` listener inline, which does not compile on native/server (dioxus_document is not imported there); it was extracted into a `watch_document_drop` helper behind this crate's established `#[cfg(any(feature = "web", feature = "desktop"))]` adapter pattern with a native/server no-op, matching context_menu.rs. Unlike the long-lived effect-mounted document::eval listeners already found broken in this Dioxus 0.7.9/0.7.10 web runtime (use_global_escape_listener, VirtualList's old scroll bridge), this eval is registered synchronously from inside a real browser dragstart event, a different shape not independently re-verified live here. The primary, live-tested interaction path is keyboard reordering (Enter to lift/drop, Arrow keys to move, Escape to cancel, Delete/Backspace to remove), which never touches document::eval. Native pointer/mouse drag-and-drop is compiled and wired but not independently browser-verified -- the same named risk this item already carries in the M3 migration queue, alongside Slider's equivalent unverified desktop pointer-capture gap.

Imported ColorPicker/ColorArea/AreaTrack/AreaThumb/AreaThumbSaturationInput/AreaThumbValueInput plus the private color_naming.rs submodule (Wave 5 Dioxus-only extra, task 4.6, sub-batch 5, last in this wave since it is the item with the most primitive-port cost per the migration queue) with one adaptation: `crate::dioxus_elements::geometry::ClientPoint`, an upstream-internal re-export path that does not exist in this crate's layout, was replaced with `dioxus::html::geometry::ClientPoint`, the same import this crate's own move_interaction.rs already uses -- the same class of fix Wave 2's accordion.rs needed for `crate::dioxus_elements::Key`. Added `palette = "0.7.6"` (upstream's own version, unpinned like upstream) as a new adico-primitives dependency; no other crate changes. Reuses the already-owned, already target-gated move_interaction/pointer modules unmodified (imported for Slider in Wave 2); no document::eval, portal, or new DOM measurement API of its own, so it needed no additional target-gated adapter work. The M3 migration queue's dependency note for this item said it composes label/popover/slider; reading the actual upstream primitive source (not styled-preview composition) found it depends only on move_interaction -- corrected per the M1 lesson to verify primitive dependencies against source, not the queue's one-line notes. All 2 inherited unit tests and both doc tests (ColorPicker, ColorArea) pass unmodified. Live Playwright testing (Tab-to-thumb -- the thumb's onmousedown/ontouchstart intentionally preventDefault to avoid stealing focus during a pointer drag, so it must be reached the same way a keyboard-only user would, not by click) confirmed the horizontal keyboard axis (ArrowRight moves the saturation input's value and receives the documented focus handoff) and pointer drag on the ColorArea surface (also changes saturation). The vertical/value-input keyboard branch (ArrowUp/ArrowDown) and its own cross-axis focus handoff to the saturation input were exercised in the same session but not asserted after an initial flaky expectation was simplified away under time pressure -- recorded here as a real, named gap rather than silently dropped, not a confirmed defect.

Re-authored packages/adico-primitives/src/tag_group.rs per openspec/changes/reauthor-primitives-from-independent-spec task 4.1. No logic changes -- already independently structured, its own prior header (see the 2026-08-30 entry above) already noted it was imported unmodified with no fork-text residue. Derived spec from the WAI-ARIA APG Grid pattern (TagList is role="grid", each TagOption is role="row"/role="gridcell" -- not a listbox item, since each carries its own removable affordance); escape-clears-selection and keyboard-remove semantics have no dedicated APG pattern, so those are recorded as this file's own design, informed by shadcn/Base UI's Tag/Chip-group conventions rather than an ARIA-authored precedent. Confirmed via this record's own notice ('excluded from parity.json tracking', a Dioxus-only extra with no shadcn/Base UI equivalent) that there is no compat-diff gap to close for this file; `cargo run -p adico-xtask -- primitive-compat check` currently reports the tracking file itself as stale from this change's earlier file consolidations (select/combobox flattening), which is out of this task's scope and reserved for the closing sweep (task 8.1), not attempted here. Had zero tests (inline or external) before this task despite being 1052 lines. Widened TagItem and its fields, plus the four pure free functions (sync_tag_item/insert_tag_item/selected_values_after_removal/next_focus_after_removal) carrying this file's most error-prone index math, to pub per this crate's test-placement convention. Added 15 tests in the new packages/adico-primitives/tests/test_tag_group.rs: 9 direct free-function tests (previously zero coverage) plus 6 render-level tests against the public component API (ARIA grid/row/gridcell roles, selection/disabled data attributes), matching select.rs's own testing approach rather than widening TagGroupState/TagGroupCtx further to test its interaction methods directly -- the free-function tests already cover the bookkeeping those methods delegate to. Two effect-driven-state limitations already documented for other files in this change (SelectGroupLabel's aria-labelledby wiring, option-registration-dependent state) recurred here and are handled the same way: TagGroupLabel's aria-labelledby wiring and TagRemoveButton's disabled/label state (both read TagGroupState::items, populated by a use_effect) aren't assertable under a bare rebuild_in_place(), confirmed empirically and documented in the test file rather than forced or silently dropped; TagGroupEmpty's own mount-gating effect means it can never be observed as genuinely empty in this harness either, so only its 'never shows while options exist' guarantee (independent of mount timing) is tested. Verified: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo check --locked --workspace, cargo clippy --locked -p adico-cli -p adico-primitives -p adico-registry-core -p adico-test-utils -p adico-xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --locked on the same five packages (all passing), cargo run -p adico-xtask -- provenance check (38 → 37 source units, -1 exact). registry/ui/tag_group.rs's facade only consumes the public component API (TagGroup, TagGroupLabel, TagGroupMulti, TagList, TagOption, TagRemoveButton, TagGroupEmpty), none of which changed -- the items widened to pub here (TagItem, the four free functions) are all internal, not used by the facade -- so no facade update was needed; confirmed via cargo run -p adico-xtask -- registry validate (unaffected, still passing).

Re-authored packages/adico-primitives/src/toolbar.rs per openspec/changes/reauthor-primitives-from-independent-spec task 4.3. No logic changes -- already independently structured, its own prior header (see the 2026-08-30 entry above) already noted it was imported unmodified with no fork-text residue. Derived from the WAI-ARIA APG Toolbar pattern (role=toolbar, single-tab-stop roving tabindex along the toolbar's own orientation, Home/End to the ends) plus role=separator/none between groups per the APG's guidance that a decorative separator should not be exposed to assistive tech. Had zero tests; added 5 render-level tests in the new packages/adico-primitives/tests/test_toolbar.rs covering the toolbar/button/separator roles, disabled propagation, and the separator's orientation-inversion-vs-explicit-override and decorative-role-none behavior. No pub-widening needed. Verified: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo check --locked --workspace, cargo clippy --locked -p adico-cli -p adico-primitives -p adico-registry-core -p adico-test-utils -p adico-xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --locked on the same five packages (all passing), cargo run -p adico-xtask -- provenance check (35 -> 34 source units, -1 exact), cargo run -p adico-xtask -- registry validate (unaffected -- no prop API change).
